title: Paramedical and Mental Health Practice Platform Competitive Landscape

scope.description: Software vendors that compete for the same customers and jobs as Health Cloud Initiative (HCI), the Dutch healthcare software group modeled in this domain: paramedical practices (physiotherapy, exercise therapy, speech therapy, occupational therapy, dietetics, podiatry, rehabilitation) that need an agenda, EPD, measurement instruments, Vecozo declarations under GDS801, LDF delivery and a patient app; independent GGZ practitioners, GGZ institutions and youth care providers that need an EPD or ECD for the zorgprestatiemodel and municipal contracts with ROM, a client portal and blended care; and the e-health content and patient-environment budget that surrounds both. HCI is included as the modeled company so that the other players' figures can be read against its own 40,000+ professionals and 4 million+ patients.
inclusionLogic: paramedical practice EPD and practice management systems (Intramed, Fysiomanager, Crossuite, James Software) that a physiotherapy practice owner or allied health therapist compares with HCI One, FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura and Evry when choosing or switching practice software - the head-to-head segment in which HCI claims to support one in four Dutch paramedics

GGZ institution EPD and ECD suites (Nedap Ons, SDB Groep USER, PinkRoccade GGZ, Adapcare, Nexus Nederland, Medicore) that the 50 largest GGZ organisations and mid-sized institutions run, and that HCI CRS meets in institutional tenders; their client portals (Caren, Karify, Wellbee) also compete with Quli and the CRS client portal

GGZ practice EPDs (Madeware Medikad, Praktijkdata, Axians Zorg GGZ) built for independent practitioners and smaller GGZ organisations, the segment where HCI CRS sells on zorgprestatiemodel declaration correctness, integrated questionnaires and a client portal

e-health platforms (Minddistrict, Therapieland) that supply questionnaires, treatment modules and client apps into every major GGZ EPD, including HCI CRS, and therefore compete with Embloom, Emogy and Quli for the e-health and client-environment budget even while integrating with HCI

geographic focus on the Netherlands, where Dutch-specific content (Vecozo, GDS801, zorgprestatiemodel, LDF, MedMij, NEN 7510) decides selections; Crossuite is included as the Benelux multidisciplinary platform that most resembles the HCI One ambition
notes: Business stats are only included when they were found on official company websites (home, about and product pages), official newsrooms and press releases, the investor Vortex Capital Partners' pages, or - for market share - the M&I/Partners GGZ EPD inventory on mxi.nl and the Marktdata physiotherapy survey; each stat preserves the company's reported scope and period, and players for which no official figure could be verified (James Software, Praktijkdata, Axians Zorg GGZ) carry a description only.

Market-share figures are third-party inventories with a narrow scope: the M&I/Partners 2025 EPD inventory covers the 50 largest GGZ organisations by revenue (data as of 1 July 2025: SDB Groep 15 or 30 percent, Nedap 14 or 27 percent, PinkRoccade 7 or 14 percent, Adapcare 6 or 12 percent, Nexus 5 or 10 percent, others 3; client portals Caren and Karify 22.5 percent each, Quli 4 percent or two organisations) and says nothing about independent practitioners, where HCI CRS is strongest; the 53 percent Intramed share is a calculated figure from a 2017 Marktdata survey of physiotherapy practices and is dated.

Vendors report at very different scopes: Nedap counts care organisations and professionals across long-term, disability and mental health care; Crossuite counts practitioners across 13 countries; Adapcare and Minddistrict count platform users; Therapieland and Embloom count programmes and questionnaires; HCI counts professionals and patients across all labels. None of these figures is directly comparable with HCI's 40,000+ professionals and 4 million+ patients.

Several players sit inside larger groups: Intramed is a product of Convenient B.V.; USER and Karify belong to SDB Groep (USER developed by Avinty, part of SDB Groep since 1 April 2023); PinkRoccade GGZ is part of TSS (Total Specific Solutions); Adapcare is part of CareRatio; Nexus Nederland belongs to the German NEXUS group; Nedap Ons is a unit of the listed Nedap N.V.; Axians Zorg belongs to VINCI Energies. Group-level figures are labeled with that scope.

HCI's reported turnover of about EUR 20 million in late 2023 and the 30,000+ providers reported in September/October 2023 come from trade-press coverage without a retained official URL and are therefore mentioned in the description only, not recorded as business stats; the June 2022 investment figures are recorded from the Dutch IT Channel report of the company announcement with that scope stated.

Physitrack, Physiotrack and Fysio AI are exercise and AI partners integrated in HCI's paramedical labels (Physitrack lists eleven Dutch EPD integrations including Intramed, Incura, Abakus, Fysiomanager and SpotOnMedics) and are not competitors; Physitrack's 2026 comparison of Dutch physiotherapy software is used only as a third-party listing reference. Minddistrict and Therapieland integrate with HCI CRS and are listed because they compete with Embloom for the same e-health budget.
The official website of PinkRoccade GGZ is recorded as found in the domain research (pinkroccade-ggz.nl) and remains to be confirmed; its statistics come exclusively from the M&I/Partners inventory.

players.name: Health Cloud Initiative (HCI, modeled company)
players.description: Health Cloud Initiative (HCI) is the modeled subject of this domain: a Dutch healthcare software group that, under the mission 'Better care, made easy', delivers practice management and EPD software to paramedical practices (HCI One, FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, Evry, ParaNICE), the HCI CRS EPD to GGZ and youth care providers, the Uw Zorg Online and Quli patient environments and personal health environment, and the Embloom, Emogy and NICE Connect e-health propositions, all on a NEN 7510 and ISO 27001 certified open cloud platform. It has been built since a 2021 Vortex Capital Partners buyout with founder Eric de Boer through more than 14 add-on acquisitions (Incura, CRS, FysioRoadmap, Winbase, Ensemble/Evry, Footfit/PodoFile, NICE Software, Uw Zorg Online, Quli, Praktijkinfo, Embloom, SpotOnMedics, Trompbx, LogicData, Abakus, Edevop), reported a turnover of about EUR 20 million in late 2023 and has been led by CEO Robin Dunki Jacobs since 1 May 2025. Its current programme, HCI One, consolidates the acquired paramedical labels on the web-based FysioRoadmap foundation discipline by discipline without a forced migration deadline. It is listed here so that the other players' figures can be read against its own 40,000+ professionals and 4 million+ patients.

players.name: Intramed (Convenient B.V.)
players.description: Intramed is the practice software of Convenient B.V. in Moordrecht and the largest incumbent in Dutch physiotherapy practice software by the only published, and dated, measure: one EPD family (Intramed Compleet, Web, OnLine, Plus and Basis) for physiotherapy, podiatry, speech therapy, occupational therapy, GGZ, dietetics, exercise therapy, skin therapy, haptotherapy and osteopathy, extended with HealthTrain e-health, the MijnZorgApp patient app, Fysio.AI documentation, Intramed Insight and ParaBench benchmarking, the AfsprakenApp, a GGZ practice dashboard, Intramed Financieel and D-Pay payments. Convenient presents itself as the first practice software supplier certified for NEN 7510 and holds ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 27001, and offers a three-month free trial. A 2017 Marktdata survey calculated a 53 percent share among physiotherapy practices, a dated third-party figure that still frames the market HCI One must win: Intramed competes head-to-head with FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics and Incura on multidisciplinary breadth, AI documentation and the patient app, while HCI counters with the consolidated HCI One platform, the Uw Zorg Online front door and billing services.

players.name: Fysiomanager
players.description: Fysiomanager is a Heerenveen-based, fully browser-based EPD and practice management system for paramedics that bundles the agenda, dossier and declarations with FM-VideoConsult, online scheduling, the MijnZorgtoegang patient portal, FM Analytics, a Twinfield accounting link and iDEAL/Wero payments, with multi-location use included in the subscription. It is NEN 7510 and ISO/IEC 27001 certified and publishes a customer satisfaction of about 90 percent. Because it also integrates with SpotOnMedics and Intramed, it appears both as a direct alternative for the physiotherapy practice owner choosing between FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics and HCI One, and as a neighbour in the same integration ecosystem (Physitrack, Twinfield, Vecozo); HCI's answer is the breadth of HCI One and its patient front door rather than price.

players.name: Crossuite
players.description: Crossuite is a Belgian-Dutch cloud practice platform for nine disciplines including physiotherapy, speech therapy, psychology, podiatry and dietetics, sold across the Benelux and beyond with agenda, dossier, invoicing and patient communication in one subscription. It reports 10,000 practitioners in 13 countries, 98 percent customer satisfaction and 18 years of operation. Its multidisciplinary, cross-border positioning is the closest analogue to HCI One's ambition of one platform for every paramedical discipline, but it does not lead with the Dutch-specific depth on which HCI's labels compete (GDS801 declarations through Vecozo, LDF and Keurmerk delivery, the Uw Zorg Online front door), so in the Netherlands it competes mainly for small multidisciplinary practices and solo allied health therapists who value simplicity and cross-border reach over Dutch-specific compliance depth.

players.name: James Software
players.description: James Software is a Dutch paramedical EPD and practice management package that is listed among the physiotherapy software options in Physitrack's 2026 comparison of Dutch EPD systems alongside Intramed, Incura, Abakus, Fysiomanager and SpotOnMedics. It competes for the same physiotherapy practice owners and allied health therapists that HCI One, FysioRoadmap and SpotOnMedics target, typically on ease of use and price for smaller practices. No business statistic could be verified on an official James Software page within this domain's research scope, so its entry carries a description only.

players.name: Nedap Ons (Nedap N.V.)
players.description: Nedap Ons is the electronic client record suite of the listed Nedap N.V. in Groenlo, used across long-term care (VVT), disability care (GHZ), GGZ and home help (HBH), and it operates the Caren client and family portal. Nedap reports more than 1,900 care organisations and approximately 400,000 care professionals on Ons, and the M&I/Partners 2025 inventory counts 14 of the 50 largest GGZ organisations (27 percent) on Nedap, closing in on the market leader after GGZ Friesland switched to Nedap, with the Caren portal at 22.5 percent of those organisations. For HCI this is the dominant alternative when a mid-sized or large GGZ institution selects an ECD, competing with HCI CRS on institutional scale, integrated portal and ecosystem (Therapieland integrates with Ons), whereas HCI CRS, Embloom and Quli target GGZ practices, youth care and institutions that want an EPD with e-health and a PGO front door.

players.name: SDB Groep (USER EPD and Karify)
players.description: SDB Groep is a Dutch care software group with more than 45 years in care that owns the USER GGZ EPD (developed by Avinty and part of SDB Groep since 1 April 2023) and the Karify client portal and e-health environment. The M&I/Partners 2025 inventory places SDB Groep as market leader with 15 of the 50 largest GGZ organisations (30 percent) and the Karify portal at 22.5 percent, although it lost GGZ Friesland to Nedap in 2025. It is the incumbent institutional EPD that HCI CRS meets in large GGZ tenders and, through Karify, a competitor for the client-portal and blended-care role that Quli and Embloom play in HCI's GGZ proposition; HCI positions CRS as the all-in-one EPD for practices, youth care and institutions with integrated e-health rather than as a separate portal product.

players.name: PinkRoccade GGZ (Total Specific Solutions)
players.description: PinkRoccade GGZ, part of TSS (Total Specific Solutions), supplies the mijnQuarant EPD and the mQ suite to GGZ institutions, including Parnassia Groep (on the mQ suite) according to the M&I/Partners 2025 inventory, which counts 7 of the 50 largest GGZ organisations (14 percent) on PinkRoccade. It is a large-institution specialist that competes with HCI CRS mainly in the upper segment of institutional tenders rather than among independent practitioners. HCI CRS, with Embloom and Quli, competes on integrated e-health, a modern client portal and a consolidated data platform rather than on installed base in the top-50 institutions. The official product website is recorded as listed in the domain research and remains to be confirmed.

players.name: Adapcare (Pluriform Zorg, CareRatio)
players.description: Adapcare in Ede, part of CareRatio, develops the Pluriform Zorg ECD and the App Anne client app for GGZ, disability care, youth care, social support (WMO) and long-term care, and reports more than 55,000 users. The M&I/Partners 2025 inventory counts 6 of the 50 largest GGZ organisations (12 percent) on Adapcare. Its cross-sector ECD competes with HCI CRS at GGZ institutions that also run youth care and WMO contracts, exactly the municipal-contracting segment in which CRS positions its Jeugdwet and WMO declaration support; HCI differentiates with the integrated Embloom questionnaires and interventions and the Quli PGO rather than with sector breadth.

players.name: Nexus Nederland
players.description: Nexus Nederland, the Dutch arm of the German NEXUS group, offers a modular EPD/ECD for GGZ institutions next to its hospital products. The M&I/Partners inventories show it losing ground in GGZ, from 7 of the 50 largest organisations in 2024 to 5 (10 percent) in 2025. It competes with HCI CRS only in institutional tenders, and its shrinking GGZ footprint is one of the openings HCI can target with CRS, Embloom and Quli as a modern, e-health-integrated alternative for mid-sized institutions.

players.name: Medicore
players.description: Medicore in Utrecht (Kanaalweg 29) positions itself as the complete and open ECD for clinical and outpatient GGZ, youth care and independent clinics, with the Mijn Medicore portal, a Zorgapp, the UP environment, an API platform and the Wellbee client portal, and a partner ecosystem of more than 20 vendors for AI agents, speech-to-text and e-health (Therapieland integrates with it). It is the most direct like-for-like competitor of HCI CRS among mid-sized GGZ organisations and independent clinics that want an open, API-first EPD with a client portal. HCI counters with the in-house Embloom content library, SmartAI voice-to-text inside CRS and the Quli PGO, while Medicore relies on its open partner platform for the same capabilities.

businessStats.value: 20+ partners for AI agents, speech-to-text and e-health on the API platform

players.name: Madeware Medikad
players.description: Madeware's Medikad is an affordable EPD for independent psychologists and GGZ therapists that also serves physiotherapy, speech therapy, youth care and occupational therapy practices, with built-in questionnaires (SQ48, CQi, HoNos, 4DKL), Vecozo declarations under the zorgprestatiemodel and the GDS801 paramedical standard integrated, and a three-month free trial. It competes with HCI CRS at the low end of the independent GGZ practitioner segment and with Incura and HCI One among small paramedical practices, on price and simplicity. HCI positions CRS with Embloom's 500+ questionnaires and 450 interventions, the client portal and SmartAI voice-to-text as the richer alternative for practices that grow into multidisciplinary or contracted care.

businessStats.value: 3 months free trial

players.name: Praktijkdata (Telasoft)
players.description: Praktijkdata, developed by Telasoft, is a fully web-based GGZ EPD for independent practitioners and GGZ organisations that covers the zorgprestatiemodel, youth care and WMO contracting, Vecozo declarations, a client portal and e-health. It is a direct alternative to HCI CRS for the independent GGZ practitioner and small GGZ organisation, the segment where the 2026 mandatory referral date and the end of the transitional benefit make declaration correctness decisive. HCI differentiates CRS with the integrated Embloom library, Quli and the multi-label data platform; no business statistic could be verified on an official Praktijkdata page within this domain's research scope.

players.name: Axians Zorg GGZ
players.description: Axians Zorg, the healthcare unit of the VINCI Energies ICT brand Axians in the Netherlands, offers an ECD for private practices and for mid-sized and large GGZ organisations in adult and youth GGZ. It spans the same range as HCI CRS, from the independent practitioner to the institution, and brings the backing of a large ICT services group with hosting and integration services. HCI competes with a more product-led proposition: CRS plus Embloom, Quli and the Uw Zorg Online front door as one integrated GGZ stack. No business statistic could be verified on an official Axians page within this domain's research scope.

players.name: Minddistrict
players.description: Minddistrict is an Amsterdam e-health platform for mental health care with modules, diaries, questionnaires, video calling and secure messaging, reporting more than 250,000 users, ISO 27001:2022 and NEN 7510-1:2017 certification and CE marking as a Class I medical device, with customers such as GGZ Delfland, GGZ NHN, Lentis and Tactus. It is both a partner (it integrates with HCI CRS) and a competitor of Embloom and Emogy for the blended-care content and client-environment budget of GGZ institutions, and of Quli for the client-facing app. HCI's counter is that Embloom's 500+ questionnaires and 450 interventions are fully integrated in its own EPD rather than delivered as a separate platform.

businessStats.value: ISO 27001:2022 and NEN 7510-1:2017 certified; CE Class I medical device

players.name: Therapieland
players.description: Therapieland in Amsterdam calls itself the largest e-health platform of the Netherlands, with more than 300 online programmes and more than 200 questionnaires, integrated with HCI's GGZ EPD, Nedap Ons, Medicore, Careweb, Medicom and Ksyos and partnered with QuestManager. Like Minddistrict it is simultaneously an integration partner of HCI CRS and a competitor of Embloom for the e-health content and ROM questionnaire budget of GGZ institutions, POH-GGZ practices and independent practitioners. HCI's positioning is the EPD-native Embloom library and Emogy client app, while Therapieland sells vendor-neutral content across every major GGZ EPD.
